```{r}
#| include: false
library(knitr)
library(dplyr)
source("02_analyse_licenses.R")

# numbers for the method text
readme_presence <- read.csv(file.path(MAT_DIR, "osf_readme_presence.csv"))
strata <- read.csv("data/manual_check_strata.csv")
pairs <- distinct(object_licenses, doi, osf_project)
n_shared_ids <- sum(table(pairs$osf_project) > 1)

# pairs without a row in the deposit's documentation coding, by object type
doc_llm <- read.csv(file.path(MAT_DIR, "osf_documentation_llm.csv"))
doc_missing <- distinct(osf_files, doi, osf_project) |>
  anti_join(doc_llm, by = c("doi", "osf_project")) |>
  left_join(distinct(object_licenses, osf_project, holder_type), by = "osf_project")
```

## Method

**Objects.** We checked every OSF id in the deposit's `osf_file_downloads.csv`:
`r n_distinct(pairs$osf_project)` distinct objects, linked as `r nrow(pairs)` paper and
object pairs by `r n_distinct(pairs$doi)` papers (`r n_shared_ids` ids are linked by two
papers). A link to a single file is resolved to the project or registration that holds it,
the same rule as in Quintana's `collect_osf_documentation.R`.

**Population.** The `r nrow(papers)` papers in `osf_readme_presence.csv`, the paper's
denominator for documentation: empirical papers sharing on OSF with a readable file
listing.

**Sources of a license.**

- *OSF license field* of each linked object, mapped to OSF's license names. Components
  carry their own license, so all components below a linked object are read, at any depth.
  Copyright-holder names are not stored, only whether one is given.
- *LICENSE files*: file names containing `license` or `licence`, or starting with
  `COPYING` or `COPYRIGHT`, in the deposit's file listing. The listing covers components at
  any depth and add-on storage such as GitHub; for registrations it covers only OSF
  storage, not components.
- *GitHub add-ons*: an OSF project can mirror a GitHub repository as storage. We record the
  license GitHub detects in the repository and count it like a LICENSE file. GitHub's
  `NOASSERTION` (a license file it cannot match) counts as licensed, like "Other" on OSF.
- *READMEs and descriptions*: the description of every object and of its direct
  components, and the README files of the `r sum(readme_presence$has_readme)` papers whose
  file listing has one (file names matching `readme`, `read me` or `read_me`, as in
  Quintana's `analyse_osf_readme.R`). The deposit lists file names without ids, so the file
  tree is walked again, including components at any depth, until all listed READMEs are
  found. PDF and Word files are converted to text. Every passage containing `licen[sc]`,
  with 200 characters on each side, is coded by hand (see below).

**Licensed paper.** A paper is licensed if any linked object or component has a license in
the OSF field, if there is a LICENSE file or a licensed GitHub add-on, or if a passage is
coded as stating a license. OSF's "No license" counts as unlicensed, "Other" (a custom
license) as licensed. We also report results for the OSF license field alone, the only
machine-readable source and the one shown on the project page.

**License types.** A paper can have more than one license, e.g. CC BY for data and MIT for
code. `license_types` in `data/license_by_paper.csv` lists all of them as SPDX ids (OSF
field, GitHub, coded passages), `osf_license_types` the OSF field only. The type of a
LICENSE file in the OSF listing is not read.

**Download models.** We add `licensed` to the paper's models of total and peak single-file
downloads. `02_analyse_licenses.R` loads `pred_prepare_data()` and `pred_build_dm()` from
Quintana's `analyse_download_predictors.R` instead of copying them, so population,
predictors and coding are the paper's. Without `licensed` the models reproduce the
published estimates. Further models add documentation and preregistration as covariates.

## Coding schemes

### License mentions

Each row of `data/license_mentions.csv` is one description or README with at least one
mention (`r nrow(mentions)` rows). Re-running `01` keeps the coding and leaves new passages
empty; `02` warns if any are uncoded and counts them as no license.

| Column | Coding |
|---|---|
| `states_license` | `yes` if the text states a license for the shared materials or for part of them (e.g. one tool); `no` for other uses of the word: licenses of third-party data or software (Matlab, LDC corpora), or "license" in another sense. |
| `license_name` | SPDX ids, several separated by `; ` (e.g. `CC-BY-4.0; GPL-3.0`). |
| `coding_note` | Reason for unclear cases. |

### Manual check

`03_sample_manual_check.R` drew `r nrow(strata)` papers, stratified so that error-prone
cases are covered. It includes every paper licensed only through a child component, a
LICENSE file or a README. The sheet is in random order and does not show our coding. Each
paper is coded in `data/manual_check.csv` by opening its OSF links.

```{r}
strata |>
  count(stratum, name = "papers") |>
  knitr::kable()
```

| Column | Coding |
|---|---|
| `license_osf` | `yes` if a linked project or registration, or one of its direct components, shows a license on its OSF page; else `no`. "No license" counts as `no`. For a link to a single file, check the project or registration holding it. |
| `license_osf_name` | The license shown, as on OSF or as SPDX id (e.g. `CC-BY-4.0`, `CC0-1.0`, `MIT`). |
| `license_other` | `yes` if a license is stated anywhere else: a LICENSE or README file, the project description, the wiki, or a deeper component; else `no`. |
| `license_other_where` | Where: `file`, `readme`, `description`, `wiki` or `component`. |
| `checked_on` | Date of the check (licenses can change after the crawl). |
| `notes` | Anything unclear. |

`04_evaluate_manual_check.R` compares this coding with ours: agreement and kappa for the
OSF license field, and per stratum how often a license is stated somewhere we do not look.

## Limitations

- Licenses are read at the crawl date, not at publication; authors can add or change a
  license later.
- OSF asks for a license when a registration is created, and *Psychological Science*
  requires an open license for submissions from 2024. Both raise the 2025 rate without an
  author choosing a license, so rates are also reported with registrations left out.
- GitHub repositories linked in the paper or the OSF description, rather than connected as
  storage, are not checked. Many of them are third-party tools (e.g. PsychoPy) whose
  license says nothing about the shared materials.
- Papers linking private projects through view-only links are not covered: the keys are
  redacted in the deposit, and those papers are outside the population.
- READMEs and descriptions are only searched for "license" or "licence". A statement like
  "data: CC0" without that word is missed, as are licenses in the wiki, in files not named
  README, and in scanned PDFs. READMEs are read only for papers whose file listing in the
  deposit has one, and not all listed READMEs could be found for one registration.
- All associations with downloads are observational.

## A note on the deposit

`r nrow(doc_missing)` of the paper and object pairs in `osf_file_downloads.csv` have no row
in the deposit's `osf_documentation_llm.csv`
(`r sum(doc_missing$holder_type %in% "registrations")` of them registrations), from
`r n_distinct(doc_missing$doi)` papers. For these objects, no description or wiki was
assessed.
This may be intentional and does not affect the license analysis.
